speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the onset and severity of your right flank pain, and have you noticed any blood in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any nausea or vomiting along with the pain, and does the discomfort radiate toward your groin? Have you had a fever or chills recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience a burning sensation when you urinate, and have you noticed any fever or chills recently? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis shows Reddish appearance, WBC 10-20 /HPF, RBC Too numerous to count, Nitrites Negative, Leukocyte_Esterase Positive.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recurrent UTIs and leukocyte esterase, I suspect a chronic infection like xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis or an obstructing stone. REQUEST TEST: CT_Urography

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT urography is normal, we need to rule out mucosal or glomerular pathology. Do you have a history of smoking, and have you experienced any weight loss or night sweats? REQUEST TEST: Cystoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Renal_Ultrasound
Given the normal CT and cystoscopy, I need to evaluate for structural abnormalities or masses that might have been missed, such as a renal cyst or tumor.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since structural and infectious causes appear ruled out by normal imaging, I must investigate glomerular or systemic etiologies. Do you have a history of high blood pressure or diabetes, and have you noticed any swelling in your legs or foamy urine? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Creatinine_and_eGFR

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the persistent hematuria and flank pain with normal imaging, I need to rule out glomerular disease or vascular issues. Have you noticed any joint pain, skin rashes, or hearing loss, and do you have a family history of kidney disease? REQUEST TEST: Urine_Protein_to_Creatinine_Ratio

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recurrent UTIs, hematuria, and flank pain with normal imaging and labs, I suspect an underlying structural or infectious anomaly not yet identified. DIAGNOSIS READY: Renal Papillary Necrosis
